notes_for_editor: No NRHP nomination text (not digitised; NPGallery lists 'Sautter, L. & Co.' as architect, evidently the lens maker). Pre-1891 annual reports are not in the corpus, so the 1827-1880 chronology rests on Lighthousefriends (facts only, quoting Board reports and papers second-hand) and the historical society. Disagreements stated in text: first tower material (stone per 1827 contract vs wooden per society); tract gift date; fog signal 1896 vs 1897 (Board report says opening of navigation 1897); second dwelling 1906 vs 1907; automation 1981 vs early 1970s; owner village vs town; William Montonna's start (obituary 1 April 1896 exam; roster assistant 1897) and pennant (index 1912-17 vs obituary 1922); Cratsenberg start (roster 1865, obituary 1866). Edward Sweet: roster gives 1960-1967 as head keeper, Lighthousefriends says he transferred in 1958; his earlier stations come from Lighthousefriends only. The roster's Harry L. Klein/Howard Seaton 'at least' spans are archive-documented spans. Report volumes cited by scan page only where the tool confirmed it; printed page numbers for 1891-92 (p.133) and 1893-94 (p.140) unconfirmed. Hours of fog-signal operation: 1899 report ~160 h, 1900 ~257 h. The 1896-97 report covers fiscal year ended June 1897. No wrecks tied to the point were found. The 'Coast Guard' roster lines (1950s-1971) are archive-listed personnel, not matched to dwellings. Corrections: none; USLHS and record agree on position. Verifier 2026-10-27: Cratsenberg's Watertown link dropped (obituary says only he came to Watertown as a young man); 1899 and 1900 reports both carry the shared-dwelling sentence; Miss Esther May entry is undated in the report.
